title: Isolation Hardware Sorter
description: Eleven job-site descriptions, dealt in a shuffled order, are placed in ten bins: open, housed, restrained and seismic spring isolators, snubber, thrust restraint, isolation hangers, isolators directly under the fan, isolation rails and isolator mounting angle. Two attempts per card with a 'look for' hint; mastery is 9 of 11 on the first attempt, and the summary lists the missed descriptions with their reasons.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Isolation hardware: spring types, motion limiters and mounting styles
learningObjectives: The learner will classify eleven job-site descriptions by the isolation hardware FanPedia calls for, with at least 9 of 11 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: open, housed, restrained and seismic spring isolators

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); placements and verdicts announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed chip, bin and feedback borders pair with colour; a wrongly chosen bin is disabled and its aria-label says 'not this one'; keys 1-9 and 0 place the card, Enter goes to the next card; focus moves to Next card after a verdict.

controls.label: 1-9, 0: the ten bins
controls.purpose: Place the face-up card in that bin (keys 1-9 and 0)

controls.label: Next card / Finish
controls.purpose: Turn up the next card; after card 11, show the summary (Enter)

controls.label: More missed
controls.purpose: Summary only: turn the page of the missed list when it does not fit

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Deal all eleven cards again in a new order and clear the score

rules: Each description has exactly one correct bin; bins can receive more than one description (items 5 and 6 share a bin).
Cards are dealt in a shuffled order; two attempts per card; no partial credit.
A wrong first placement returns the card with a 'Look for <feature>' hint; a second wrong placement moves it to its correct bin and shows the reason.
Mastery is 9 of 11 correct on the first attempt.
limitations: The 30-inch impeller in item 5 is illustrative.
Real specifications may combine several of these items on one fan.

sources: FanPedia: The Fan & Blower Encyclopedia, pp. 133-135 and 196-197

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classify realistic job descriptions by the one feature that names the hardware (enclosure, direction of support, where brackets attach)
keyQuestions: What encloses the spring, and does it limit motion?
Does the fan stand on the floor or hang from structure?
Which device limits motion instead of isolating?
commonMisconceptions: A snubber and a seismic spring are the same device.
Any spring restrains a fan against airflow forces (open springs do not).
Every fan can sit on isolators bolted directly under it.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 11'; mastery is 9 of 11 on the first attempt.
Summary list of descriptions missed on the first attempt, with their correct bins and reasons.
